thesis: Validate whether 'INT3 + RMS residual beats INT4 alone' generalizes across 7 models, or is Mode-1-specific.
headline_finding: INT3+RMS is universally BETTER than INT3 alone (19-94% ΔPPL reduction), but strictly BEATS INT4 alone only on the Mode 1 case (Qwen2-7B). This is logically consistent with the two-mode theory: INT4 is broken on Mode 1 (valley of death), so INT3+RMS can surpass it there. On Mode 2 where INT4 is clean, INT3+RMS narrows but doesn't close the gap.

claim_1_universal_int3_improvement.statement: Per-channel RMS residual correction universally improves nsep+pchan INT3, across all 7 models in our sample. Mode 1 sees 94% damage reduction; Mode 2 sees 16-72%.
claim_1_universal_int3_improvement.evidence: INT3+RMS < INT3 alone on every single measured model.
claim_1_universal_int3_improvement.cost: +1 bit/value + D FP16 per channel (~256 bytes/head metadata). Effective 4+ε bits.

claim_2_mode1_specific_int4_dominance.statement: On the Mode 1 case (Qwen2-7B), INT3+RMS (+0.025 ΔPPL) strictly surpasses INT4 alone (+0.054). This dominance is Mode-1-specific: INT4 alone suffers from the INT4 valley of death on Mode 1 models, so INT3 (which escapes the valley) + residual can win despite being a lower base precision.
claim_2_mode1_specific_int4_dominance.implication: The 2.2x precision improvement of INT3+RMS over INT4 on Qwen2-7B is a direct consequence of the INT4 valley, not a universal superiority of residual correction.

claim_3_mode2_int3_rms_loses_to_int4.statement: On all 6 Mode 2 models, INT3+RMS improves over INT3 alone but does not surpass INT4 alone. Mode 2 models have monotonic bit-width scaling; INT4's cleaner levels beat INT3's loose levels + residual correction.
claim_3_mode2_int3_rms_loses_to_int4.note: Mistral-7B is closest to a tie (+0.024 vs +0.018, 1.3x). All gaps in absolute terms are tiny (<0.1 ΔPPL).

mode_aware_deployment_framework.description: A mode-aware deployment strategy emerges naturally from this analysis

if_K_at_L0_gte_15x.rationale: Escapes the INT4 valley of death; best quality at sub-5-bit budget

if_K_at_L0_lt_10x.rationale: Simpler than residual; strictly better on Mode 2 models

scientific_conclusion: The INT3+RMS residual correction provides two distinct benefits: (1) a universal improvement over INT3 alone at a modest extra cost, and (2) a Mode-1-specific rescue that surpasses INT4 alone by exploiting the INT4 valley. This pattern is internally consistent with and further supports the two-failure-mode framework of modeq's companion paper.
